I personally love using PODspy, Pinterest & Printful together! 🤑 Great way to make money online! Love print on demand! ⚠️ Make sure you link your Printful account to a store! For example, when you sign up for Printful you can choose stores to link it too, like Etsy or Shopify! This way when you make a sale on your Etsy store, Printful can get to work and print the design and put it in the frame for you & they ship it out to the customer!  👌🏼 When it comes to making money selling on Etsy, make sure you're doing research and making products people want to buy! Look for proof like best-seller badges on the Etsy listings. Also look for 20+ carts on the listing!  😏 If you aren't making money online with print on demand then I can guarantee it's either you aren't marketing your product consistently of even at all, have bad mockups or you're making random things that have no proof people want to buy. You could also simply have bad designs which is where using tools like @PODspy | AI POD Design Tool come in handy. It’s so fun to boss around the AI 🤭 👩🏻‍🏫 I don't say this to be mean, I say this to help you! 🤭How to make money online selling products on Etsy you didn't make yourself using the done for you designs & print on demand method!  👇🏼Read for a step by step!  🙌🏼 How Print On Demand Works:  1. Do Some Quick Product Research - Look for popular items people are buying, like wall art, t-shirts, sweatshirts, phone cases, candles, mugs, or tote bags.   - Use tools like erank, Google Trends or browse online shops to see what's trending. I also look for inspo on Pinterest all the time! I like to use Everbee to see how much money a product is making on Etsy.  2. Create Your Design  - Get done for you designs on ctrl-alt-design.com  - Or create your own. Make your design fun, eye-catching, or niche-specific. Keep it simple and high-quality!   3. Sign Up on Printify  - Create a free account & make sure you connect your account to a store. Examples being Etsy or Shopify. You are walked through how to do this when you sign up, don’t worry it’s easy and fast.  4. Choose a Product on Printify   - Browse the product catalog for posters, t-shirts, hoodies, candles, hats, mugs, phone cases & etc.   - Select the product you want to sell.   5. Upload Your Design   - Click on the product to customize it.   - Upload your design.   - Position and resize it to fit the product nicely.   6. Fill Out Listing Details  - Write a catchy product title and description with keywords.   - Set your price (consider costs and your profit margin).   7. Publish Your Product  - Remember to connect your online store (Shopify, Etsy, etc.) with Printful . This makes it so whenever you make a sale, Printify knows instantly so it can print the design on the product for you and send it to the customer for you!  - Publish your product so it’s live and ready for customers.   8. Market Your Product - Share your product on social media, use Pinterest, create ads, or tell friends. Make videos of your product or make Pinterest pins.  - Focus on your target audience to attract more buyers. Not a must but it can help!  #howtomakemoneyonline #sidehustle #onlinesidehustle #printondemand #digitalproducts

Act as an experienced Etsy seller, greeting-card designer, digital product creator, and Etsy marketing strategist. I want to create a greeting card that I can sell on Etsy for $14. My goal is to create a product that looks professional, feels worth the price, and has a clear target customer. Give me a complete product blueprint that includes: 1. Product Concept * Give me 5 greeting card concepts that have strong emotional appeal and could realistically sell for around $14. * Identify the target customer for each. * Explain why someone would pay $14 for it instead of buying a cheaper card at a retail store. * Rank the 5 ideas from strongest to weakest. 2. Choose the Best Idea     Select the strongest concept and explain why you chose it.     Give the card a memorable product name. 3. Card Design     Give me the exact design concept, including: * Front cover text * Inside message * Back-of-card text * Recommended colors * Font styles * Layout * Graphics/illustrations * Overall aesthetic * Recommended card size * Whether it should be funny, sentimental, elegant, minimalist, etc. 4. Create the Actual Product     Give me step-by-step instructions for creating the finished greeting card using beginner-friendly tools such as Canva and/or AI. Include: * Exact Canva dimensions * What template to start with * What elements to search for * What text to enter * How to arrange everything * How to create the front and inside * How to create the back * How to export the finished design * What file formats I should use 5. Make It Worth $14     Suggest ways to turn a basic greeting card into a $14 product, such as: * Personalization * Premium packaging * Envelope * Gift-ready presentation * Multiple design variations * Bonus cards * Digital + physical options * Other value-adds Be realistic about what customers would actually consider valuable. 6. Etsy Listing     Write the complete Etsy listing for me, including: * SEO-optimized title * Description * 13 Etsy tags * Keywords * Product features * Personalization instructions * Shipping information * Processing time * FAQ * Call to action Make the listing sound natural and human rather than stuffed with keywords. 7. Product Photos     Give me a shot list of at least 8 Etsy listing photos I should create.     For each photo, tell me exactly what should be shown and what text, if any, should be included. 8. Pricing     Break down how I should price the product at $14.     Explain estimated costs, Etsy fees, shipping considerations, and approximate profit per sale. Clearly separate assumptions from actual Etsy fees. 9. Launch Strategy     Give me a simple 7-day launch plan for getting my first Etsy sales, including: * What to post on TikTok * What to post on Pinterest * How many Etsy listings I should create * How to get initial traffic * What I should do every day 10. Final Checklist     End with a step-by-step checklist starting with “Create the design” and ending with “Make the listing live.” Keep the instructions beginner-friendly and extremely actionable. Assume I have never created or sold a greeting card on Etsy before. Do not just give me general advice. Give me specific examples, exact wording, dimensions, design instructions, and actions I can follow to create the actual product and list it for sale.

i have also been a victim of the online chaos 🙋‍♀️ that makes you think you need to be doing 10X the volume, trying a bunch of different product types, and jumping into a bunch of different niches just because it’s Q4 as someone who has been selling print on demand products on etsy for almost 4 years now, the things that help you have a great Q4 are not any different than the things that help you have a great Q1, Q2, and Q3 the only thing that’s different about Q4 is that there are more shoppers buying products (hello holiday season!)  when more people are shopping, your chance of getting sales goes up 💸 and the way you “take advantage” of that is by creating products that people are searching for and getting them listed about 60-90 days in advance. and that is not a “special Q4 strategy” that is what you should be doing january through september too! you don’t need to try a different product type. you don’t need to jump into a bunch of new niches. you don’t need to list a thousand ornaments yesterday (lollll)  you just need to keep doing the same consistent, simple, boring things that actually get results there is no magic trick for Q4 and there is nothing different or unique that you need to do to have a successful one okay, end rant 😉 (ty for coming to my talk)

videos.caption: Finding an Etsy trend is easy.  Knowing WHEN to use it is the real skill. 🔥 One of the biggest mistakes I see Etsy sellers make is jumping on something after it has already been everywhere for months. I want to know how long the trend has been building before deciding whether it belongs in an Etsy shop. Look beyond the hype and pay attention to timing. Getting there earlier gives you more room to actually build around the trend.
